extracted.intended_audience: PR agencies, brand communications teams, and entrants preparing submissions for the Cannes Lions PR Lions awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and judging criteria for submitting PR work to the Cannes Lions PR Lions awards, covering eligibility, category selection, written submission questions, evidence requirements and how entries will be judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging criteria weights
rubrics_metrics.description: A number of criteria will be considered during judging, weighted as follows: 20% idea; 30% PR strategy; 20% PR execution; 30% impact and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These weights determine how the jury allocates score across the submission sections: creative idea (20%), PR strategy (30%), PR execution (20%), and impact/results (30%). Ensure your written answers and evidence emphasise the higher-weighted areas (strategy and impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy rooted in earned media
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategy rooted in earned media that has real impact, beyond likes and impressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jury values campaigns where earned media (journalism, organic PR coverage) drives meaningful outcomes rather than purely vanity metrics. Demonstrate how earned media contributed to business/reputational goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling at the core
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that has storytelling at its core and establishes, protects or enhances the reputation and business of an organisation or brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use narrative to show the problem, insight, idea and outcome. Storytelling should be evident both in written submission and case film to help the work stand out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong insight
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong insight that underpins the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show the insight that motivated the strategy and creative idea — why the target behaved as they did and how the idea exploited that. Provide evidence or research where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impressive execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Impressive execution that brings the idea to life effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how the concept was implemented across channels, the creativity in execution, and any adaptations made during rollout. Use concrete examples and assets where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real results linked to objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Real results that link back to the objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link performance metrics directly to the objectives you selected. Provide verifiable evidence of impact (brand metrics, behaviour change, sales, ROI, policy change, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Considered strategy at every touchpoint
rubrics_metrics.description: Considered strategy, thoughtfully designed at every touchpoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how each channel/touchpoint contributed to the strategy and how the audience journey was designed for impact and coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury: determine most impressive element
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the most impressive part of your campaign and find a category that showcases it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the category that foregrounds your strongest contribution (idea, strategy, craft, use of data). Submitting into the best-fit category improves chances of recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury: provide tangible results
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide tangible results that demonstrate impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative and qualitative evidence should be included. The jury will scrutinise the credibility of claims — supply verifiable data and be prepared to back it up in confidential evidence if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury: provide global context
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide context throughout your entry so the international jury understands significance and relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain market size, cultural specifics, baseline metrics, and why the results matter in that context. Avoid assuming jury familiarity with local nuances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury: storytelling in written submission and case film
rubrics_metrics.description: The Jury look at hundreds of pieces of work, use storytelling in the written submission and case film to help your work stand out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a clear narrative arc in both written and film materials, emphasising insight, idea, execution and measurable outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility period requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Work will need to have been executed during the eligibility period of 06 February 2025 - 09 April 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only work executed in this timeframe qualifies — ensure dates in your submission and supporting evidence demonstrate execution within the eligibility window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry frequency limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The same piece of work can be entered up to four times in PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may submit the same campaign in up to four PR entries, but observe additional section-specific restrictions. Plan category choices to maximise fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section A single-entry exception
rubrics_metrics.description: The same piece of work may only be entered once in ‘A. PR: Sectors’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If entering sector categories (A01–A07), do not submit the same piece multiple times within this section; choose the single most appropriate sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section E independent-agency restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Work in Section E: Excellence in PR Craft can only be submitted and paid for by independent PR agencies or companies owned by a PR network or independent PR network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only eligible independent agencies/networks may submit to Section E; the same piece can be entered only once in each category within this section. Confirm agency status before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of impact & verifiable evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: You'll be required provide proof of impact, supported by verifiable evidence; this information will not be shared with the Jury, but will be used to verify claims made in your entry materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare confidential evidence (third-party data, analytics screenshots, sales figures, signed attestations) to substantiate claims. Misrepresentation or wilful omission may result in withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior executive approval
rubrics_metrics.description: You'll also be required to provide details of a senior executive from both the brand and the entrant company (CEO, CMO or equivalent) who can formally approve the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure named executives are prepared to sign off on claims and submissions; provide accurate contact details as part of the entry process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional supporting materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional supporting materials to provide additional context with your entry can also be uploaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use optional uploads to provide creative assets, case film, press cuttings or other evidence — but ensure core claims are present in the written answers since judges rely on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save progress before checkout
rubrics_metrics.description: You can fill in the form in any order and save your progress at any time while it’s still in the pending stage. However, please only check out when your entry is 100% complete as no changes can be made to your entry once you’ve clicked 'Submit' and 'Checkout'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use drafts to refine answers; once submitted no edits allowed. Finalise and verify all content before checking out and paying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question: Why is this work relevant for PR?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why this work is relevant for PR. The word limit for this section is 100 words. This question is compulsory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Succinctly state the PR relevance — what reputation, perception or stakeholder outcome the work targeted and why it belongs in a PR awards context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question: Brand Context
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide any brand and cultural context that would help the jury understand any cultural, national or regional nuances applicable to this work. Word limit: 250 words. Compulsory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline why the work was created for this brand, in this market, at this time, and describe cultural/market conditions that shaped the idea and its reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question: Objectives (link results to objectives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the objective(s) that were most important when creating this work. For the jury to accurately assess the work, they must first establish its objectives. As you progress through the entry system, you must link your results back to each objective selected. There is no word limit. This question is compulsory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose relevant objectives (e.g. overachieve on brand metrics, change consumer behaviour, create sales growth, improve brand health, long-term growth) and ensure all reported results map directly to these objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question: Summary of the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a summary of your entry. Describe background, context, creative challenges and analysis of effectiveness; describe how objectives were met. Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise overview linking the problem, insight, idea, execution and measurable outcomes. Use this to set the scene for the jury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question: Describe the creative idea (20% of vote)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the work crosses boundaries, evokes surprise, transcends the original challenge, incorporates breakthrough thinking and demonstrates how the idea was designed to earn attention from the target audience. Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address: boundary-crossing, attention-capturing, transformative qualities and originality. Provide brief examples of how the idea delivered attention and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question: Describe the PR strategy (30% of vote)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider how effectively the concept was brought to life; which PR implementation strategies were employed; channels used and their appropriateness; scale of execution relative to objectives; and whether the execution adapted to unexpected challenges. Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain strategic rationale, channel mix, targeting, media relations approach, timing and contingency responses. Highlight strategic thinking and planning that enabled impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question: Describe the PR execution (20% of vote)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider how effectively the concept was brought to life; what specific PR implementation strategies were employed; which channels were utilised; scale in relation to objectives; and adaptations to unexpected changes. Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail tactical steps, creative assets, earned media activations, influencer/community management, events/stunts and practical executional choices that delivered the strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question: List the impact and results (30% of vote)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer back to the objectives selected. Consider performance against brand metrics, change in consumer behaviour, indications of sales success, brand health improvement, potential changes in government regulations or societal/economic events. Word limit: 250 words. Compulsory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide measurable data (awareness, engagement, sales, ROI, share, behaviour change), timeframes, attribution methods and any secondary effects (policy change, regulatory impact). Link metrics to objectives clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI usage disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Was Artificial Intelligence (AI) used in the work or the entry materials? If yes, you must disclose how it was used, including tools, extent of AI use, data sources/inputs and where they originated. Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow LIONS Integrity Handbook guidance on acceptable AI usage. Be explicit about tool names, outputs used, training/data inputs and degree of human oversight. Omission may lead to withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability context
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline how the piece aligns with the brand's sustainability strategy: environmental cost, evidence for sustainability claims, long-term commitments and benchmarks used to measure success. No word limit. Optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide lifecycle environmental considerations, verifiable evidence for sustainability claims, and show alignment to broader brand targets such as AdNet Zero commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity, representation and accessibility (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the brief, what consideration was given to representation/diversity of the team(s) and accessibility in the work and what role did DEI thinking play? No word limit. Optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe team composition, inclusive practices, accessibility features and how DEI thinking informed creative decisions and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential information field
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are additional results you wish to disclose to the Jury but prefer to keep confidential, provide them in this field (150 words). Optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place sensitive supporting evidence here (detailed sales figures, contracts) that you do not want publicly visible but will be reviewed by judges for verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category selection: A. PR: Sectors guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Sector categories for consumer goods, healthcare, automotive, travel/leisure/retail/restaurants & fast-food chains, media/entertainment, consumer services/B2B, and not-for-profit/charity/government. The same entry can be submitted only once in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the sector that best matches the product/service. Note exceptions (e.g. fast-food entries go to A04; charity/NFP in A07). The same work may only be entered once in Section A.

rubrics_metrics.name: A01. Consumer Goods criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: All fast-moving and durable consumer goods; entries should reflect relevance to consumer goods markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include category-specific context such as product type, distribution and consumer behaviour to justify sector fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: A02. Healthcare criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Pharma, OTC drugs, wellness. If the work has been created for a Charity/NFP then this should be entered into A07.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail regulatory considerations, medical evidence and ethical constraints relevant to healthcare communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: A03. Automotive criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Vehicles, other automobiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight product lifecycle, purchase cycles and automotive-specific channels or partnerships used.

rubrics_metrics.name: A04. Travel, Leisure, Retail, Restaurants & Fast-Food Chains
rubrics_metrics.description: All transport- and travel-related services, entertainment and leisure services, shops, restaurants and fast-food chains. All fast-food entries should be entered into A04.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how campaign addressed footfall, bookings, visits or consumer experience metrics relevant to these sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: A05. Media/Entertainment criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Music, film, television, publications and media, books, news, digital platforms and other media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate relevance to media audiences, editorial partnerships and publicity outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: A06. Consumer Services / Business to Business
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial public services, legal, financial, B2B technology, consultancies and professional services, internal and corporate communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how PR objectives and tactics were tailored for corporate/B2B audiences and decision-making cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: A07. Not-for-Profit / Charity / Government
rubrics_metrics.description: Government, public information, NGOs, military, charities, non-profit organisations. All corporate social responsibility work should be entered in the relevant sector and/or F07.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain public interest objectives, stakeholder engagement and social impact measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: B01. Social Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrating public relations and social media storytelling that build brand awareness and advocacy. The work should demonstrate how social media was harnessed to increase brand awareness and relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide social metrics, platform strategy, creative formats and examples of community response or advocacy built.

rubrics_metrics.name: B02. Community Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognising the development, maintenance and nurturing of brand relationships. The work should demonstrate how engaging with a brand's online community/targeted audience built its reputation and established trust and authority within the online community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show moderation strategy, response times, community growth/engagement metrics and examples of relationship-building outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: B03. Real-Time Response
rubrics_metrics.description: Real-time social activity designed to respond to and engage in the conversation around world events, public affairs and other real-world, real-time activity in a creative and meaningful way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate speed, relevance, editorial/creative judgement and impact on conversation or reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: B04. Content Creation & Production
rubrics_metrics.description: Content created and produced to entertain, inspire or educate. The work should demonstrate how the content created was audience-relevant and engaging as well as in line with brand messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide production details, distribution approach and audience engagement metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: B05. Content Discovery & Amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognising a creative approach to content amplification and distribution in order to reach the largest potential audience. The work should demonstrate how a combination of earned, paid, shared and owned media contributed to increased brand engagement and awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail the mix of paid/earned/owned/shared channels, targeting/placement tactics and resulting reach/engagement uplift.

rubrics_metrics.name: B06. Innovative Use of Influencers/Creators
rubrics_metrics.description: The creative and innovative use of influencers/creators to drive brand message and awareness to a specific audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain selection criteria for creators, creative brief, partnership model and measures of effectiveness (authenticity, engagement, conversions).

rubrics_metrics.name: C01. Research, Data & Analytics
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and data-led or actionable insights that provide a meaningful contribution or input to a public relations programme. The work should provide evidence of research or insight, quality of thinking and the development of a strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include methodology, data sources, how insights were derived and how they informed strategy/creative decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: C02. PR Effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognises creative work that has a proven impact on business and reputation. The work should provide results data, as well as details of measurement tools and analysis methods used to evaluate results. Consideration will be given to tangible business results and the quality and quantity of media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply KPIs, measurement frameworks, attribution approaches, media quality metrics and business outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: D01. Media Relations
rubrics_metrics.description: PR that puts journalism at the forefront of the campaign, with evidence of a high degree of innovation intended to engage, educate or influence editorial. The work should explain the relevance of media outcomes, including depth, quality and messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show press strategy, media targets, pitch examples, earned coverage quality (depth, placement), and how coverage supported objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: D02. Use of Events & Stunts
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that uses stunts, events, event sponsorship, competitions, promotional games, street art, guerrilla marketing, launch parties, live shows, live streamed events, festivals, concerts, sporting events, etc. within traditional, digital and new emerging environments to build the value and reputation of a brand or communication project as part of a wider public relations strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain event objectives, audience activation, experiential design, media amplification and measured impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: D03. Launch / Relaunch
rubrics_metrics.description: Work created to launch or relaunch a product or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate pre-launch planning, launch mechanics, media and influencer activation, and early performance indicators tied to launch goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: D04. Brand Voice & Strategic Storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Customised strategies designed to communicate a particular point of view/story of a brand/organisation in a consistently relevant way and to build an emotional connection with employees, shareholders and customers alike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show messaging frameworks, tone of voice, consistency across channels and evidence of emotional resonance with stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: D05. Use of Technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing or new technology that pushes the boundaries of digital innovation to execute or support a PR campaign (AI, VR, virtual worlds, robotics, gadgets, wearables). Does not include prototypes of early-stage technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe technological role, user experience, integration with PR strategy and measurable impact. Exclude immature prototypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: D06. Employee Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications programmes or initiatives designed to inform, educate or inspire employees - engaging internal communities and cultivating strong team dynamics. The work should demonstrate innovative approaches to engaging staff, driving organisational goals and building employee loyalty and satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide internal KPIs, participation rates, satisfaction metrics and examples of behavioural or performance impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: E01. Corporate Image, Communication & Reputation Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that builds the image/raises the profile and shapes the perceptions of a corporate brand, organisation or corporation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate strategic positioning, reputation metrics, stakeholder engagement and measurable reputation outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: E02. Public Affairs & Lobbying
rubrics_metrics.description: Work planned to influence or inform the public policy agenda using either lobbying or wider public affairs strategies, as well as political or ballot initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain policy objectives, stakeholder mapping, engagement tactics, evidence of influence and ethical/regulatory compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: E03. Crisis Communications & Issue Management
rubrics_metrics.description: The planning and/or handling of the consequences of a crisis or an issue that may affect a company’s credibility and reputation. The work should demonstrate evidence of the planning and/or implementation of a crisis communication strategy and how the desired outcome was achieved. The content of entries in this category can be kept entirely confidential and used for judging purposes only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timeline, escalation processes, stakeholder communications, outcomes and lessons learned. Use confidential field for sensitive evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: E04. Internal Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging internal communications and activities including change management to connect employees with a company identity or message; should demonstrate measurable results, employee satisfaction and business growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include participation metrics, sentiment measures, retention or productivity impacts and alignment with organisational change goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: E05. Sponsorship & Brand Partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that utilised sponsorship and/or partnership programmes in order to meet specific awareness/business goals as well as to enhance the image of a brand, organisation or corporation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail partner selection, activation mechanics, co-created assets, mutual outcomes and measurement of partnership ROI.

rubrics_metrics.name: F01. Local Brand
rubrics_metrics.description: Work for brands distributed solely within a specific locality. The work should resonate with a clearly defined, local target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain local audience insight, market-specific adaptations and local media/community engagement metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: F02. Challenger Brand
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands that have creatively adapted their approach in response to competitor pressure by challenging the status quo to create game-changing work that uses progressive thinking and innovative creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how the campaign differentiated the brand from competitors and the competitive impact achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: F03. Single-Market Campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that aired or ran in a single country / region / market. The work should describe how the campaign was designed for the specific target market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline cultural tailoring, channel selection and market-specific performance metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: F04. Social Behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Work inspired by a specific audience or community, relying on identifiable social behaviour. The work should demonstrate how leveraging insights into consumer behaviour can create a powerful connection with a brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the social behaviour observed, how it was leveraged and evidence that the behaviour was influenced as intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: F05. Use of Humour
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that celebrates the art of humour in branded communications. Infusing wit, satire, and cleverness into campaigns that provide amusement and create memorable, laughter-inducing connections with audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate comedic insight, cultural sensitivity, executional timing and audience reception/engagement metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: F06. Breakthrough on a Budget (budget details)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative use of modest budgets and/or resources in relation to the market and/or industry to create maximum impact. Provide budget details: overall budget, cost breakdown, how campaign maximised reach vs expenditure and significant impact of this adjustment. Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply budget figures, spend allocation and demonstrate efficiency metrics (reach per spend, earned media value vs paid spend). Use confidential field for sensitive financials if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: F07. Corporate Purpose & Social Responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose-driven work/brand activism that addresses social, ethical and environmental issues. The work should demonstrate how the brand’s purpose has created value and affected communities by connecting customers to culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe purpose-rooted strategy, community impact, measurable social/environmental outcomes and evidence supporting claims. Not-for-profit work may also be entered in A07.

rubrics_metrics.name: F08. Market Disruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands that have creatively adapted their strategy in response to local / regional / global issues, embracing new ways of delivering their brand while showing consideration for the consumer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show strategic adaptation, innovative commercial or delivery models and resulting market impact or consumer behaviour shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: F09. Cultural Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that honours marketers who craft strategic solutions rooted in the lived experiences of culturally grounded communities. Insights should reflect customs, behaviours and traditions shaping perspectives on identity and show how this drove growth and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific cultural insight, community engagement approach, authenticity safeguards and measures of resonance with the cultural audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific compulsory question reminders
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain categories have additional compulsory short questions (e.g., C01, C02, F01–F09) with 150-word limits focused on evidence of research, effectiveness, local resonance, budget detail, cultural insight, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer category-specific prompts concisely and provide the requested evidence. These are compulsory for the listed categories and will be considered by the jury when assessing the entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of confidential evidence for jury verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Jury will not see proof-of-impact evidence uploaded for verification, but organisers will use it to verify claims. Confidential entries (e.g., crisis communications) can be kept entirely confidential for judging purposes only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place sensitive metrics, contracts, or third-party data in confidential fields. Ensure accuracy and be prepared for possible follow-up verification checks.
